## Result and scope

Problem **30004900 / OWR-8415356-006**, rank 1186, remains **UNRESOLVED after approach 1 (1/5)**. This draft adds the complete mathematical report and full independent audit as a proof-only edition. No novelty, new universal square-root upper bound or fixed-dimensional super-square-root lower bound is claimed.

Every full-dimensional d-polytope with n ≥ d+2 vertices is the coordinate projection of a full-dimensional inscribed (d+1)-polytope with exactly n vertices. The explicit sign choice handles possible affine degeneracy, and radial exposure gives the exact vertex count. Projection monotonicity yields F_d(n) ≤ I_(d+1)(n). Hence the inscribed and unrestricted square-root assertions, each quantified over all fixed dimensions, are equivalent.

The **dimension shift and simplex exception are essential**. This is not a same-dimension equivalence and supplies no dimension-independent constant. An inscribed three-dimensional square-root bound would imply the unrestricted polygon bound. The established inscribed dimension-two theorem does not already do so.

The same lift puts at least n−1 vertices in an arbitrarily small fixed positive-radius spherical cap after scaling. This identifies a limitation of proofs requiring well-distributed vertices; it does not disprove the conjecture.

The original report body is byte-identical. All mathematical audit paragraphs and substantive source findings are retained. The audit required no mathematical corrections and accepted only the partial structural reduction. Narrow inventory/history edits remove original input and package fingerprints and make omitted-evidence boundaries explicit. This is independent AI-assisted mathematical auditing, not human peer review or proof-assistant formalization.

## Sources and status limits

The source question appears in Sauermann's contribution, joint with Kwan and Zhao, in [Oberwolfach Report 53/2021, printed p. 2929](https://ems.press/content/serial-article-files/46931), published in 2022. The checked [Kwan–Sauermann–Zhao manuscript](https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.08836v3) distinguishes its universal cyclic-polygon bound, probabilistic fixed-dimensional sphere theorem and growing-dimensional lower bound. The comparison with [Shitov's published polygon bound](https://londmathsoc.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1112/plms.70137) is limited to theorem-statement and bibliographic verification, with no claim that it is the best available bound.

Source inspection dates, raw public PDF hashes and sizes, successful checks and retrieval limitations are retained. Packaging did not retrieve or rehash sources, repeat their reading or perform a new literature review. The bounded source-status and attribution searches do not certify exhaustiveness or novelty.

## Edition verification and publication boundary

The exact nine-file allowlist, UTF-8/JSON parsing, manifest identities, local links, retained mathematical text, non-executable modes and an addition-only patch replay were checked locally. The public MANIFEST.json identifies the included edition files. These are packaging checks, not a new mathematical certification or an omitted computation rerun. No numerical experiment is used to justify the universal partial conclusions.

Fresh bounded repository checks found no target-ID/source-ID or inscribed-polytope duplicate and no target directory on the inspected main commit. A broad spherical/extension search returned an unrelated spherical-area result; it was excluded by mathematical comparison. These checks do not prove absence from deleted or unindexed history.

Only authored mathematical text, the full mathematical audit and public verification metadata are included. No copied source PDFs, images, extracted source text, datasets, check programs, fixtures, private sources, private personal data, local source paths, excluded-file hashes or private coordination records are published. No QUEUE edit, turn-count change, additional proof-search approach, merge, release or outreach is part of this draft.
